site.title: Awesome AI Architecture
site.tagline: Curated by failure mode, not vendor category.
site.description: A curated, opinionated map of AI infrastructure tooling, organized by the specific failure mode each tool addresses — with an explicit exclusion criteria, not an exhaustive link dump.

articles.title: Watchtower and Moat
articles.hook: Agent security isn't a tool choice — it's a layering problem. LLM-layer guards and runtime sandboxes solve different failure modes. Pick one, you get a speed bump. Stack both, you get an architecture.

articles.title: Smoke Signals in Production
articles.hook: Multi-agent frameworks aren't ranked by what they build—they're ranked by what you can see when they break.

articles.title: Where the Sandbox Ends
articles.hook: Every sandbox you deployed is theater if your LLM guardrails can't stop the prompt that makes the agent ask the sandbox to do the wrong thing.

articles.title: Where Agents Break Free
articles.hook: Prompt guardrails don't stop rm -rf / — most agent stacks secure the LLM layer and leave the runtime wide open.

articles.title: Multi-Model Routing & AI Gateway Tools, Mapped by Failure Mode
articles.hook: Multi-model gateways aren't about accessing more models; they're about surviving the inevitable failures, schema drift, and cost spikes of the ones you already use.

articles.title: Multi-Model Routing & AI Gateway Tools, Mapped by Failure Mode
articles.hook: AI gateways have split into two camps: zero-ops marketplaces for teams wanting unified model access, and self-hosted control planes for teams treating routing as infrastructure. The middle is empty.

articles.title: LLM Evaluation & Testing Tools, Mapped by Failure Mode
articles.hook: Most "LLM evaluation" tools are observability dashboards wearing a testing costume — this list keeps only the ones that can fail a build.

articles.title: Cost-Governance Tooling for AI Systems, Mapped by Failure Mode
articles.hook: Most AI cost tooling monitors spend after it's gone — the tools that matter let you set a ceiling before the bill arrives.
